utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner with Denise Gustin case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you good afternoon. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman with Milan Trbojevic and Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon to you too. Before we start, I have on my desk some what appear to be -- these are your documents, do I take it? They are the Defence documents, no, that they are going to use? All right. So, yes, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, two matters. I'm afraid that I've managed to exhibit last Friday documents which had already got exhibit numbers and the confusion is bad enough without adding to it. So could I, Your Honour, P1581 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- has already been exhibited as P138. So can we just make sure that doesn't appear? P1585 has already been exhibited as P908. P1587 is P1416. And P1588 is already exhibited as P655. So we just make sure that we don't have the same two documents or the same document with two different numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've already got the Defence re-exhibiting some of our documents with their numbers, and I'm grateful, may I say, to Ms. Jevtovic for pointing that out, that we had already exhibited them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, if you could print out this page and hand it over to my secretary so that she will make the necessary adjustments after the sitting? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the second matter, may I ask to go into private session very quickly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are now going to continue with the examination-in-chief of the witness we have been hearing the last three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, to you, Mr. Selak, Colonel Selak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. I hope you had a good weekend. We will be proceeding with your testimony. We won't finish today but probably we will finish tomorrow. And before we continue, please can I ask you to repeat your solemn undertaking to tell us the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel. You may sit down. Ms. Korner will be proceeding with her in chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, good afternoon. Could you have back, please, the newspaper article that you were looking at on Friday? I'm not sure we gave it an exhibit number. Yes, we did. 1593. When we concluded on Friday, I was asking you about General Talic having told the reporter about the transformation of the army. Now, if we look at the next question by the reporter, he referred to groups of armed people wearing other uniforms and an increase in shooting, planting explosive devices, and robberies. Went on to say, "Some people seemed to believe, mistakenly one would say, that this is something to do with the army, but the fact is the army seems to have nothing to say about this." And Talic said, "There must not be any armed or trained units outside the corps and the Territorial Defence except for the legal security forces, i.e., the police. That means no Serbian Defence Forces, or similar organisations outside the JNA. I have warned that such forces must not control the city." And then he talked about the military police or the police force cooperating with the military police. Then the explosions. And said, "In my opinion, what we have here are show-downs between groups and individuals and the forces of the security services centre should deal with it. If they need help from the military police, they only have to ask." Now, Colonel Selak, I think you dealt with this earlier but as far as you could see, did either the security services, the members of the SUP or the military police, do anything to control the SOS?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Talic did say that the civilian police needed to do whatever was necessary to protect the town, but he did nothing concretely, that is his corps did nothing to prevent paramilitary formations from wandering about town, roaming about town, or men who had been armed about by the corps itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then he went on to deal with the strength of the Banja Luka Corps. He explained that most of the people were deserters, that is the SOS, "These are men whom we have already disarmed and arrested as paramilitary formations." Then, I think you've already dealt with whether that was correct. Then he was asked about the estimate of the critical point in the corps's zone and replied, "The Banja Luka Corps has such a large force and such an organisation that there is no risk of the corps or the people of Krajina being endangered." And again I think you dealt with that when we were dealing with your resistance group. Now, can we go, please, to the part that -- it's headed, "Europe does not want to see." And actually just before that, though, he was dealing, the paragraph begins, "The crimes committed by the Croatian Army in Kupres," and then goes on to say, "It makes me wonder all the more of the policy of the Muslim leadership in Bosnia for I believe that unfortunately, the greatest losers in this war could turn out to be the Muslims, who in fact are not interested in any division of territory and can live together with Serbs without any tension or conflict." Then, "Wherever the Serbs are the majority population, there is peace. This is an indisputable fact. Therefore, if Muslims in the Autonomous Region of Krajina turn out to be too closely linked with the headquarters of the SDA, which is not exactly inclined to peace, then there could be conflicts which would lead no where." He in fact summarising is saying that it is the Muslims who are to blame for the situation. Was this something that he expressed privately as well as publicly?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then he went on to deal with the withdrawal of the ECMM monitors. He was asked whether he had discussions with the representatives of the local Muslims, and he said that he had spoken with the Banja Luka mufti and a group of prominent Muslims from Banja Luka. And then he dealt with the Territorial Defence being divided on -- along ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I want to ask but that article. But I want you now, please, before we look at the first video clip that I want to ask you about, is -- could you have back the 1st Krajina Corps war diary, please? Have we still got the original here? I think it would be better if the officer had -- Colonel Selak had the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had a message from Mr. Ackerman that he's going to be asking about quite a lot of the war diary, so we will arrange for copies for Your Honours. It just takes a long time to print out. He doesn't need that, no, no, no. Thanks. I'll put up -- but I will ask to put up on the ELMO, please, the English translation at page 104.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you find, please, Colonel, the entry -- all right. It's not right. Page -- I'm sorry, it's page 14, not 104. And could you find, please, Colonel, the entry for the 24th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can you give it to me, please? It's not the right page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is a very long entry, I think, this one, and it records the events effectively at the beginning of what was called operation corridor. And I think on -- do we see -- can you find a part which says that "General Talic was of the view that establishing a corridor was far more important than the fall of Derventa?" I think it's right at the end of that entry.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very end, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And at 0502 hours, Major Veljko Latka [phoen] brought in helicopter, Colonel Bosko Kelecevic, Chief of Staff, and Milan Martic, a Minister of the RSK, from Knin. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you'll find it's the very last lines on the entry for the 24th of June.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here he mentions General Talic. I'm sorry, I can't find it. Kelecevic? Yes, he's mentioned here. Yes. Yes. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you already told us who Milan Martic was. Now, can I ask, please, that we play the video with the number V0002297?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we pause? Your Honours, there is a transcript for this, which has got the number 11.6 on it. No. Has it? Right. And it begins, the translation pages begin 03003505. It's headed, "RTB Belgrade Radio and Television." Yes. If we can play the video? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "More precisely at the location of the 1st Krajina Corps command where Milan Martic has just arrived, will be present at this meeting at what is being called a historic act where the decision will be taken to mount a counteroffensive to go for all or nothing. It is certain that whatever happens will be dependent on this decision. Our forces have been tasked with -- or the aim of the operation could be described as the liberation of Serbian areas, the Serbian people who live in those areas, their territory, and to do this in two stages. First by severing communications south of Derventa."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we pause the video, please and could you just roll back so that we can see the man with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel, I know it's a very bad video, but are you able to say who that is?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like Kelecevic, but it's not him, Bosko Kelecevic. I'm afraid it's dark. It's not Talic, no. Kelecevic, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We are going to in a few moments, I think see a shot of a whole lot of officers sitting around a table. If you recognise any of them, could you just say stop so that the video stops and then identify them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we can roll on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Severing communications south of Derventa along the River Bosna, Modrica, Bosanski Samac, and then in the second part of the operation, to reach the river Sava and establish the natural borders of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "The situation is a lot more than just alarming. We do not have basic foodstuffs or medicines for the elderly, sick, or infirm."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, what did you say, Colonel? Can you see Talic to the right, yes --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Talic, and to his left is Milan Martic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that what it says on the screen?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's him, I'm not sure. Yes. It says so on the screen but the picture is very dark. I can just see his hair and his uniform. And not his face really.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We heard --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could see Martic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we have the lights dimmed, it would help because there is too much light for all of us actually. Could the technicians -- yes. Perfect. And perhaps we could rewind a little bit to where we started from, and go -- proceed forward bit by bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Talic. To his left or rather on the screen it's on his right --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recognise them. I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is a very bad quality video. All right. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you can go on playing the video, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "We do not have basic foodstuffs or medicines for the elderly, sick, or infirm. They are dying every day. Children are dying, and we could not watch this misery any longer. We brought our forces here and have subordinated ourselves to General Talic. Together with the army of Serbian Bosnia, we will attempt to open a corridor and to prove to the whole world that no one can keep the Serbs in isolation, closed in."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are personnel carriers, tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, I'm sorry, you can't talk at the same time that the video is playing. If you want to say something, then you have to say, "Stop." It's not your fault. I should have explained that. Is there something you want to say?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to say that we see a column of combat vehicles, anti-aircraft weapons, a tank unit in motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we just let the rest of the video play or the part I want, and then I'll ask you some questions at the end. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, continue playing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Reporter: The penetration of the corridor began at dawn on the 12th of June this year. The clash of large military formations occurred less than five minutes after the final decision to break the Croatian Posavina storm. The liberators were met by aggressors from the 103rd and 108th Croatian Brigades and hundreds of Alija's mujahedin. In one night, Jokovac and Kotorsko fell while fighting continued at Jakes and Dobor Kula, the Ustasha stronghold near Odzak. The liberation of this area was commanded by Colonel Milan Novakovic and the legendary Milan Martic with the collaboration of the "Vukovi sa Vucjaka," the wolves from Vucjak, under the command of Lieutenant Milankovic. Colonel Novica Simic commanded a brigade of the 1st Krajina Corps at Jokovac."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Text added later] "This operation is being undertaken to widen the corridor which we need and to establish the northern border of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the right bank of the River Sava. The operation itself...part of the operation, this attack on Odzak, is unfolding in stages, as we have been informed that there are about four and a half thousand Serbian captives in the town itself. We therefore have to take that into account. We have undertaken every measure to ensure that their lives are not endangered, and we will attempt to free them as soon as possible. "Three Croatian brigades literally fled from Odzak as their stronghold of Dobor Kula fell. On the same day, the soldiers from Modrica also escaped, burning all before them and taking Serbian captives - including women and children - across the Sava. The Croatian soldiers then succeeded in setting light to part of the refinery in Modrica with rocket launchers from the Croatian side. [end of added text] The fighting for Derventa lasted for three days, Colonels Baltic and Lisica commanded the liberators' army. "The second purpose of this operation is to open a corridor towards Serbia. In this way, we shall secure the area of the Krajinas. It is easier for me to say Krajinas than the Knin Krajina and Bosanska Krajina. Thus, we shall secure the necessary raw materials for industry to work, and above all, to procure medicines and other essentials for our children and the infirm. The third aim of the operation is for us to link up with the East Bosnian Corps and to collaborate with them to penetrate to the borders of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and join them to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel, on the transcript it said that Talic was talking over that last part, but was that in fact Talic's voice or was it whoever was at the board indicating the map?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is Talic's voice. Before him, there was Simic speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And after that, Talic's voice. I recognised the voice very well. And Lieutenant Colonel was pointing from the corps command, the zones of responsibility, and the axis along which it would act to gain control of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we heard the reporter explaining that the so-called liberation of this area was commanded by Colonel Milankovic, the legendary Milan Martic, and the collaboration of the wolves from Vucjak under the command of Lieutenant Milankovic. Now, Martic, apart from being the -- one of the ministers from the Croatian Krajina, did he also have a group of fighters, paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A large number of fighters, not a group. A group implies a small number. A large number of fighters came from the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and the aim was to gain control of the corridor, Banja Luka, Doboj, towards Yugoslavia, which was of vital significance for the Banja Luka Corps, as it was the only link between the Republic of Serbian Krajina, the Bosnian Krajina, where the first corps was, and Yugoslavia. Precisely because of logistic and all other support, and the linkage of Yugoslavia with the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But what I'm interested in is this apparently shows that paramilitary formations were fighting with the 1st Krajina Corps on this occasion. Was that something that you expected to see?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why they were armed, in fact, in order to join in battle the forces of the Banja Luka Corps, because the Banja Luka Corps didn't have a hundred thousand soldiers by establishment, and the paramilitary units were joined who joined the corps for logistic support, and these columns went to Belgrade to provide logistic support for these units. I would give units, corps units, instructions. Now who they passed on the logistics support to, I don't know, but they were fully provided.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And General Talic, we heard describing at the beginning of this video clip, describing this operation, as the liberation of Serbian areas, the Serbian people, who live in this area. As far as you know, did he consider that wherever Serbs were, that was a Serbian area?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Literally so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, I'd like you to look next at another -- some parts of a very, very lengthy video, which is 3881.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video has got a transcript but it doesn't need it because it's actually subtitled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, Ms. Korner -- yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was wondering if the transcript of that last video is going to be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was going to be my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Because if not, we have a problem because a lot of it wasn't translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was going to be my question. Was 11.6 -- did you intend this to be an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour. I'm sorry, I moved on. I intend for the video to be made P1581A with the transcript 1581B. I don't know why the translation stopped in the middle but it -- why is that no good?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. How can it be B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know that but so what, all right. .1, then. 1581-1. I think it's better that the transcript and the video stay together. So if I can't have B because Mr. Ackerman says it means a B/C/S transcript, then can I have point 1 or point 2, the video 1581.1, the transcript 1582.2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1581. We had already.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know we did, Your Honour, but I just -- I would like it attached to the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was -- 1518 would according to the statement that Ms. Korner made earlier on at the beginning of the sitting revert to its original exhibit number, which was 183 or something, I can't remember now. So at the moment, at the moment, when I asked you to print out, the documents that were marked last week, 1581, 158 -- whatever, that have been highlighted, do not -- do not exist any longer, so we have blanks there which are going to be filled in now as I take it from what Ms. Korner has just stated? Yes, Mr. Ackerman? Does that confuse you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Judge, it's an enormous problem. I'm always thinking about somebody dealing with this transcript down the road who is not sitting here. If they are looking at the transcript and they come across Exhibit 1581, which we now have decided is 138. But if they come across the transcript of Friday and see 1581 and they go look for it, they are going to get a videotape which has nothing to do with it. I don't think we should be changing the numbers after the fact because it is misleading to anybody that is trying to follow the transcript. I think we have to leave them alone, even if they are duplicates.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I never heard such complete -- anybody who wants to read this transcript after will see it refers to a document. If they read it properly, they will see the exhibit number changed, but I really do not want to waste any more time on this utterly footling point. So can we make it the next exhibit number up? If we followed that and we will sort out the later -- those missing exhibit numbers later, so it will be P1594 as the point 1, for the video and P1594.1A for the transcript and B for the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just would like to say that these are not futile points. I've gone a great deal of appellate work and these things drive you crazy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The expression was footling, which is not quite the same thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move ahead. The transcript for the next video is 7. --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You don't need it, Your Honour. That's what I was about to explain. It's subtitled. Your Honour, there may be a slight hiccup because I've given the booth the various times from my television, and I hope it will work but it may not entirely. So this is the first part of the video, Your Honour, which should start from 29 minutes in. It's video 3881.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, again, could we have the lights dimmed a little bit, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Novica Simic. He was my neighbour. We lived in the same building. He was a brigade commander, later a corps commander, and later minister and member of the general staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'd like to continue playing the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know who that is, Colonel Selak?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. The face seems familiar, but it's been a long time, and I'm not quite sure. He is a colonel but -- the face is familiar but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask for the assistance of the AV because I gave them a list of the timings on it. Was that up to 34.28 minutes? If so, I don't want to play any more. And I can't remember. I suppose they have no way of telling me that. All right. Can we run it forward a bit more, please, and then I'll just see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think we can stop the video there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, that part, because then could I ask the booth to move to the next part that I've set out in the timings. But before we do that, Colonel, two things about that part of the video. We heard Talic on a number of occasions talking about the union of all Serbs, the mother country, Serbia, joining up with the mother country, Serbia, and the like. As far as you are aware, was this not just a political goal but one that he personally shared as well?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the ultimate objective of the Army of Republika Srpska, the Serb Krajina, to join up with Yugoslavia and create a joint state. I'd like to ask you for a minute to say that what General Talic just said that 11 babies died because of the shortage of oxygen was not true. Personally, I provided seven oxygen bottles for the hospital and the Banja Luka television also reported, that is informed the public. So this was misinformation intended to add up to -- to add oil to the fire, to add firewood to the fire, to stir up trouble and raise tension among the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That was in fact the next question I was going to ask you, because it's been raised a number of times already in this trial. As far as you know, is there any truth in this story that was spread that these Banja Luka babies died for lack of oxygen which was caused by the blockage of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information was taken over and carried by all the media of the Republika Srpska, in order to emphasise the importance of the corridor towards Yugoslavia and the logistic supply of the -- of all the units. In my transport columns for Belgrade, there were also civilian vehicles which were taking food and medicines, and other supplies needed for the population in Banja Luka and Bosanska Krajina. I repeat that the oxygen for the hospital I supplied, so this is merely pointing out that 11 babies died. Yes, they were tense, but it is not true that 11 babies died.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right could we move to the next part, if it's set up, which should start at around 44 minutes? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause there for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, do you know what we are looking at? We can see the burned out villages and houses.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right on the screen are the units, that is UNPROFOR men, UNPROFOR officers. On the left-hand side, I believe is Colonel -- the name escapes me but I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we take the video back? I'm still worried about the -- just to the shot before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause, yes, that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know what we are looking at? Is that Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is. I believe it is Western Slavonia. I marked some units or rather some areas in west Slavonia in Pakrac and Lipik, and I was also in Glina and towards Karlovac. And with the commander of the 10th Partisan Division, Colonel Jozsefic, I inspected, I toured this area. I cannot really say which houses are these.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we can carry on with the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we can pause it there, thank you. And then if we could move it on to the next part while I ask a couple of questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We saw also there, Colonel Selak, General Talic saying that -- words to the effect that there was a Muslim-Croat coalition to enslave the Serbian people. From what you knew of him, did he genuinely believe that, when he was saying this on television?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did believe that sincerely because he sincerely wanted for the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to come into being, and he did all within his power to attain that objective. He believed that all the means were good to achieve that objective. So they had excellent cooperation with all political structures and with the SDS in particular. And nobody opposed it because they were pursuing the same common goal, and that was the establishment of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He believed that firmly and to the very end.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have the final clip on this video, which is about some 30 seconds or so? One -- it should start at 1 hour 32.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go back slightly? I'm sorry, a bit further back than that. We just need to see the question, I think. Yes. All right. From there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. We can stop it there, thank you. Yes, that's all I require on that video. Now, Your Honour, I should add that this is a series of clips at various times assembled on one tape, and one could see clearly General Talic saying or somebody saying the third year of the war, and that was again a much later part of the show so that wasn't filmed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But two things. General Talic in that clip that we looked at referred to the Turkish converts and the Ustasha knife. Is that the sort of language you would expect from a general in the army?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is -- it was a very offensive statement, a very offensive expression, and how shall I put it, an intellectual, an accomplished man, should never allow himself to say that because he insulted the Bosniak people, the Croatian people, and did so knowingly, and he was doing it in order to mobilise the Serb people in their pursuit of their common objective.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He also mentioned that documents apparently found in Kozarac show that there was a plan to -- not specified -- but liquidate people, presumably the Serbs, going from house to house. Were you aware of any such plan by the Bosniaks in Kozarac or anywhere in that area, to go from house to house liquidating people?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a total fabrication. As a professional soldier, I'm asking you: Who is going to leave what lists of houses, especially in Kozarac, to carry lists around houses and keep them there? One can only laugh at that, because it is quite clear who this is addressed to and why. It is addressed to the people, to people who believe whatever he says, because he's their commander. So they keep up the tension. And what happened in Kozarac was the murder of over 2.500 people in three days alone, not to mention the ethnic cleansing which followed and which also meant the end of a -- much more larger number of people. And it was statements like this of generals, corps commanders, politicians of the SDS and other parties, Serb officials, they mounted the -- they led to mounting of the tension, and unfortunately prompted the Serb people to commit the crime which was committed in Kozarac and other areas. I'm not going to did go into that now. Unfortunately, such intellectuals as Talic are responsible for the genocide which took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, I want - before we look at the next video clip which is very short - to ask you to look at a new document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that video now become 1595? That's the one with the number V0003881.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, could you be shown, please, a document that has not been numbered P380? Which I don't think I put in yet. No. P380, please I'm sorry, did I say not been numbered? It has been numbered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have a P380 which has nothing to do with that. I have a P380 which is a Sanski Most document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It should be a 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It should be 308 maybe. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have a P380 which is a 1st Krajina Corps document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dated the 1st of June?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the one with a disclosure 4.627?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a 1st Krajina Corps operational report dated the 1st of June. And if you look at the third paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can put it on the ELMO, Your Honour, the English, if there is a problem. It's one of those, is it? Oh, okay. I didn't realise we had copied --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, it talks about "Groups being disarmed every day, particularly within the city itself, people who failed to respond to mobilisation or day work lose their jobs and criminal Prosecution is instigated against them. A portion of the Muslim and Croatian population is moving out and the region of Bosnian Krajina has issued a decision to facilitate such departures providing that the Serbs from Central Bosnia and places with predominantly Muslim and Croatian populations were also allowed to move out. Those departing will not be allowed to return." Now, then in the next paragraph, it deals with operations in Kljuc, and the energetic action by the 30th Partisan division resulted in the defeat and break-up of these forces in the town of Kljuc and the villages of Pudin Han, Velegic, and Donji Ramici. And then it talks about 280 enemy soldiers being captured in Kljuc and a number of them killed. Then it talks about Kamicak and Vrhpolje. And then this at the bottom: "The heaviest fighting has taken place in the area of Hambarine, Prijedor, and Kozarac. Troops under the command of the Prijedor area cleared Hambarine and Kozarac and completely destroyed one ZNG unit, black shirts, foreign mercenaries, and legionnaires. The troops have arrested more than 2.000 Green Berets, who are now in Omarska; 135 of them in Stara Gradiska; and 5.000 in the village of Trnopolje. Among the arrested is a large number of officers and organisers of paramilitary formations." And then it says at the end of this paragraph: "The troops and officers received written commendation from the corps commander for the determination, skill, and courage they had demonstrated. They are an example of how one should act while defending the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Unfortunately, eight VRS army members have laid down their lives in the fighting and 23 were wounded." Now, Colonel, you've already explained to us what happened there and about the meeting with General Talic, but I want you now, please, to look at the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could this document be made -- it's already --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can you look, please, at a short video, which bears the number V0002590? For which there is a transcript, Your Honours, marked 11.7. It's a one-page. If we could play the video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have a technical problem or what? Madam Registrar, could you -- I can't see --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Here it is. It's on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "They indulged in some birthday celebrations. First greeting his soldiers and officers, and then the numerous guests and invitees, the Commander of the 5th Kozara Brigade, Colonel Pero Colic, stated how happy he was to be with such fighters today in these difficult times of war and how together they were defending the heart of Republika Srpska. "Tomorrow, if need be, Posavina will be at Kozara, Kozara in Herzegovina, Herzegovina at Srbobran, Srbobran in Serbian Krajina and all of us together in Serbia and Montenegro as our brothers from these Serbian lands have been with us from the beginning, fighting against the Ustashas and Islam. Without this knowledge, we would not have been successful in this struggle against the entire world, where even the few friends we have are not allowed to be our friends. It is difficult to list all the places and front lines where the heroic 5th Kozara Brigade carried its flag high with honour and dignity. It should be enough to mention that it was on all the Western Slavonian front lines where we not only defended and succeeded in defending the Serbian people and the Serbian land, but contributed greatly to the organisation of the Serbian army and its bodies after...after Slavonia. The 5th Kozara Brigade, which earlier prepared and armed the Serbian people, played a great role and succeeded in defending Prijedor and the surrounding area after which we went to Gradacac and then to the Brcko front. Here we feel at home, thanks primarily to the fighters and the command of the 1st Posavina and the 3rd Semberija Brigades. Our fighters accepted...became a part of this people and that is what is most important for the defence of this Serbian land. "To the bravest and most distinguished fighters."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, we heard Colonel Colic saying at this ceremony that the 5th Kozara Brigade earlier prepared and armed the Serbian people. Were you aware that the 5th Kozara Brigade had been arming the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 5th Kozara Brigade, that is General Uzelac, asked in May, 1991, that weapons be issued to this brigade, the Territorial Defence, but the conditions were not met for its mobilisation. I refused to issue those weapons, Pero Colic -- Colonel Pero Colic, Colonel Vaso Tepsic came to me - he was the assistant corps commander for the rear - to ask for the weapons. And I did not give them to them but I called General Crmaric in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I stop you for a moment, Colonel Selak, because I think you told us about this yesterday, this incident. But what appears to be said here is that the 5th Kozara Brigade prepared and armed the Serbian people. In other words handed over weapons to non-members of this unit. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it says that it played a great role and succeeded in defending Prijedor and the surrounding area. Did this unit play a part in the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did. A direct part.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, just one further thing: Could you have back that earlier document, P380? Because there was one thing I forgot to ask you. You still have it. It's signed, we see, by Colonel Vukelic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it says at the -- in the last paragraph, "This report should be thrashed out with all the soldiers specifying that the facts it presents are more credible than those in the mass media." So it lacks certain details regarding some specific communities. Was this a regular thing, that a report on the current political and security situation would be discussed with the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this information went from the corps command and the assistant for morale, assistant corps commander for morale, down to brigade and other units, commanders, out side the brigades and the commanders of these units were to inform all their troops, all their officers, and all their men about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that last video, please, be made Exhibit 1596 and the transcript will be 1A and 1B -- 1/A and 1/B. Your Honour, it may well be that this is the appropriate time for a break because I'm moving to a couple more documents and one last video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which was 1595, then?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 1595 was the video before, 3881. The subtitled one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was -- I see. All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have a transcript for this because we had the subtitles, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There is actually a transcript, but the subtitles are there. And it is a very, very lengthy video, Your Honour so perhaps it's just as well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we break now, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to say -- I did say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 15 minutes? 15 minutes break?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman? Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, could you be given now, please Exhibit number P608, disclosure number 4.840? I want to return to the topic of cooperation, before we look at the last video. Colonel Selak, again it's a 1st Krajina Corps -- in fact an order dated the 1st of April, 1992, and it is, I think, signed -- let me just check -- is that -- actually, I think that's actually signed by General Talic himself, is it not, if you look at the last page? Or is that a "za" -- maybe it's a "za"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And it starts with describing the complexity of the political and security situation, particularly in Sanski Most, Prijedor, Kljuc, Mrkonjic Grad, and Sipovo, and then it's an order in respect of the 10th Partisan Brigade. And the order is to send it towards Sanski Most, deploy the union -- the union -- the unit in the Sanski Most, Kamengrad village area and gives it the various tasks, the military tasks, and then says, "Establish full cooperation with the organs of government in Sanski Most municipality and collaboration with the Territorial Defence and police units." Would you expect an order redeploying a particular unit to include establishing full cooperation with the political bodies?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not customary. However, it's illogical because the brigade has to cooperate both with political and police authorities of the respective municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Thank you. That's already been exhibited. So could you look, please, at one more document with the disclosure number 4.619, dated the 21st of May. Again, I think if you look at the last page of this rather lengthy document, it's been signed on behalf of General Talic?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it talks about the general mobilisation of the Serbian army within Bosnia-Herzegovina, and if we look under the words, "I hereby order: 1. Immediately establish direct contact with municipal and military and territorial organs on the ground, offering expert and material support for the mobilisation process." Now, in -- I think you may have already told us that -- this, but where a mobilisation was ordered, was it important that there was direct contact with the municipal, military, territorial organs on the ground?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is essential, because those organs had accurate records of all able-bodied men on their territory, with the exact addresses of where they were residing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then could you go, please, to paragraph numbered number 8? We see that the tasks -- until the units received concrete combat tasks, engage them in the following task, and item 4: "Establish the closest possible cooperation with the people and legal authorities within their zones of responsibility." And then finally, item number -- paragraph number 11: "Do not allow the presence of any paramilitary formations or other special organisations within the zones of responsibility. Disperse individual members amongst various units as volunteers, but if they refuse that, break them up and, if necessary, destroy them." We saw not so long ago the video showing Martic's men, I think they were called Martici, and the Wolves of Vucjak fighting with the 5th corps or the 1st corps by then. Was that -- this order to effectively disperse paramilitary units among regular units something that you would expect?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In this paragraph, it is indicated such groups should be placed under the control of the corps units. Either as volunteers or as groups. I had not heard that any such group had been disarmed, and the unit commander should have made sure that those paramilitary units had to carry out their orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So -- I'm sorry, Colonel, does that mean that this order should have meant that instead of the groups fighting as a group, like the Wolves of Vucjak, they should have been split up and dispersed into actual units?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 11 clearly says that they should be divided up and attached individually to other units or brigades of the corps, and if they don't obey, they should be disarmed. However, this was not implemented, at least I do not know of a single unit of paramilitary formations having been disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd now like to you watch part of the video -- I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May that be made Exhibit P1597?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd now like to you watch the last set of video clips. One it's V0001853. Your Honour, there is a transcript which has got the number 5.21 on it. Your Honour, part of what we are going to see on this video has been seen on another video. Clearly the same clips were recorded by different people. But parts we haven't seen before.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "That is what they do to their own, and as to what they are capable of devising for others, it is evidenced. "...The Muslim and Croat extremists have under their control just two more villages in Kotor Varos municipality - Vecici and Ravne. The chief organisers of the resistance in these villages are well-known criminals Muhamed Berbic and Mehmed Sadikovic. They have many wounded among them, while their food supply is almost exhausted. Vrbanjci, until recently an Ustasha stronghold, is now firmly held by the troops of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "I would like to say that we encountered an excellent spirit of cooperation among those people. Unfortunately, we had a situation where in two villages, despite an agreement that had been reached, they started shooting at units of the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, as well as members of my unit. Therefore, we had to respond accordingly. "Mr. Brdjanin, could you please tell us what the reasons are for your visit and what your view is on the latest developments in the territory of Kotor Varos municipality? "Let me tell you that being the president of the Autonomous Region Crisis Staff, it is my responsibility to tour all the front lines. I have admit that I have most frequently toured the Corridor, the passage to Serbia, but simply today's visit...the reason for this visit is that every Monday I must inform presidents of all crisis staffers about the political situation in this region. We have to clear our area, which definitely encompasses Kotor Varos and Jajce, and the most important battle being waged is the one I toured yesterday, the breakthrough to Serbia. We can see for ourselves that there is simply no point in further negotiating with those who are at war with us; those who took up arms must be defeated, must surrender their weapons, and total Serbian rule established here."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we pause the video before we move on?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What would be the importance of this speech being made by Mr. Brdjanin to Banja Luka television, Colonel Selak?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kotor Varos municipality was on the border towards central Bosnia, and the Banja Luka Corps had one of its main goals to take control of Kotor Varos, so as to link up the line towards Teslic and Doboj. Brdjanin's words were addressed not just to the combatants but also to the population, and the aim they had set themselves, they wanted to achieve, but on that day, more than 400 men were killed in Kotor Varos. That was the price. In the report of this brigade, it was stated that soldiers were killed but that is not true. The truth is that in addition to soldiers, a large number of inhabitants were liquidated too, and there are documents to corroborate this, and eyewitness testimony too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. He says that it's his responsibility to tour all the front lines. Why? Why was that his responsibility? What was the importance of him touring the front lines?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that. How could he possibly know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, of course, if it wasn't this witness, it was another -- the one before him who did hint about the importance of such visits, actually. So the -- your objection is not sustained. It's rejected.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: From -- I'll rephrase the question because -- Colonel Selak, as a soldier, what would -- or as a commander or whatever, what would have been the importance of the leader, the President of the Autonomous Region Crisis Staff touring the front lines?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was actually this same witness. You had asked him very similar, almost identical question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I had, in relation to an entry there but not quite in the same way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I'm allowing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The visit of an official, of political officials, such as the President of the Crisis Staff, for me as a unit commander, would mean a recognition and paying tribute to me for carrying out my tasks, that my unit and my soldiers had carried out the tasks assigned to, and that the people stand behind that unit. Because he represented the civilian authorities. And that is why it was very important to make visits by political bodies to all front lines. And these visits were regularly held throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we continue playing the video

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] -- "We also asked political authorities to undertake all measures in order to avoid potentially Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. inflammatory situations which could result in devastation of buildings, loss of human life, and so on. However, I have to say that the other side has, at least partially, come to terms with such activity on our part, but certain number of extremists has gone into hiding and they do not wish to be put under our control, nor do they wish to surrender their weapons. "This surprise visit to Serbian soldiers by the Krajina leadership demonstrates that there is a synchronised cooperation. In addition to activities involving liberation of Serbian territories, officers, and soldiers, members of Serbian armed units are also directly involved in establishing the Corridor towards Serbia, which is one of the greatest operations in the history of the Serbian people. "...Serbian defenders, whereas more than 65 were wounded. Just last week in this area, mostly in the villages of Vecici, Vranici, Sokoline, and Rujevica, 17 soldiers and members of the special police unit were killed. Last night's list of fatalities included Colonel Milan Stevilovic, head of the Department for Intelligence and Security Affairs of the 1st Krajina Corps; Stevan Markovic, head of the Police Department in the Banja Luka Public Security Station; Obrad Bubic, a craftsman from Kotor Varos; while Novo Petrusic, a driver, was captured and taken away. In addition, yesterday in the afternoon, Djuro Eskic, an employee of Proleter, was killed in Kotor Varos by a sniper shooting from Kotor on the left bank of the Vrbanja river. Last year during a clearing of terrain in villages inhabited by Muslims and Croats in Kotor Varos municipality, the fiercest battles were waged in the very same village of Vecici. Yesterday and today, aviation of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina took part in the final operations conducted jointly by the troops of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and special police units, firing at selected enemy targets."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can see planes bombing Kotor Varos there, Colonel. Do you know what type of bombs they were using?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Or what type of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For ground forces, tanks and APCs were used. Chemical weapons were not used, only incendiary devices. Explosives, powerful bombs, and incendiary cluster bombs. This was ordered by General Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Can you move on with the video?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The number of fatalities among the Muslim-Croat paramilitary has exceeded 300, with a significantly greater number of wounded, about 200. In yesterday's and today's combat alone, Muslim and Croat extremists had over 100 wounded and killed and about 200 wounded. Their own civilians, Muslim women, children, and the elderly are held hostage by the extremists, who tortured and kill them. Yesterday, between 16 and 1700 hours in the vicinity of Rujevica village, on the road between Maslovare and Kotor Varos extreme cruelty, enemy villains ambushed and tormented to death Stevan Markovic and Obrad Bubic, also killing Milan Stevilovic and capturing Nova Petrusic. A commemoration ceremony was held today in honour of Milan Stevilovic at the Banja Luka JNA hall. "He spent many years of his young life serving in the military police and security agencies. He selflessly took the time away from his family and generously invested his efforts towards strengthening the units and defenders of this beautiful homeland of ours. At the time of his death, he was serving as the head of the Department for Intelligence and Security Affairs in the 1st Krajina Corps, a formation he so enthusiastically supported and towards whose success he worked tirelessly. And those efforts of his were not fruitless, for he leaves behind him a corps that has no equal in Europe or the world. He lived his life and built his career in an honourable, decent, and dignified manner, while his selfless work frequently served as an example to others. He received several decorations and awards and was promoted to the rank of colonel in an extraordinary procedure. "Stevilovic was born in 1946 in the village of Motike by Drvar and through his perseverance and tireless work has grown into -- "...a courageous and valiant son of Krajina and a hero of Drvar. "Predrag Radic, president of the Banja Luka municipality, spoke of the life and achievements of Colonel Stevilovic. Colonel Stevilovic's funeral will take place tomorrow in his native village of Motike by Drvar, while a commemorative service will be held in Stevan Markovic's honour tomorrow morning in Banja Luka. "...and our crew. "The local commune of Kotor, another firm stronghold of the Ustasha on the Kotor Varos municipality, has finally been captured. Deputy commander of the special units of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre, Ljuban Ecim, will tell us how this operation was conducted. "This was definitely one of the most synchronised and most organised operations conducted on the territory of Kotor Varos municipality. Excellent results were achieved in some six hours of action under the guidance of the special unit and splendid, let me underline this, excellent assistance provided by the reserve and active forces of the Security Services Centre, many of whose members took part in combat for the first time today, but truly lived up with to the name of Krajisnik, men from Krajina, in battle. We were also assisted by a certain segment of units of Serbian forces...Serbian troops of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. With only one victim and three wounded on our side, we managed to destroy the core of the HVO and kill the self-proclaimed HVO commander, Stipo Maric, also known as Sprzo, who has up until now inflicted heavy losses on us through many treacherous ambushes. His victims included Colonel Milan Stevilovic and head of our police department, Stevan Markovic. However, justice came to collect its dues, and today we destroyed the entire group and liberated a larger portion of the town. So that now it can be said that the entire city of Kotor Varos is finally free. "Based on your assessment, what are the enemy's losses? "Well, at least 50 or so, but we won't know the real figure for a few days, because the terrain is fairly difficult to access and there are many mountain peaks. The greatest obstacle is that part of the combat was conducted in Kula and Stari Grad, where Sprzo was killed. "What would you like to tell our viewers regarding Vecici? "Well, Vecici partially got what it deserved and the rest will follow. We are going one by one, and we will get to that village. "With respect to the proposal on constituting an association of assemblies of Republika Srpska and Republic of Serbian Krajina and also the United Nations Security Council Resolution 820."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop. It's my fault. I had the microphone -- I had the microphone off. Could we run the video back, please, to the beginning of this segment and then start again? Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before we move on to this, Colonel Selak, we saw Ljuban Ecim being interviewed. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was with him twice, in the SUP building. We met there. Precisely, we talked about certain weapons, but that was at the beginning of the war in Croatia. Later on, we didn't meet again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This special unit of the CSB that he commanded, did you know anything about that unit?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received an order from the command of the 2nd Military District of Sarajevo to issue weapons and other materiel, equipment, for this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think we looked at that document or you dealt with it in your diary -- your workbook, earlier. The sort of people who were in that unit --

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- Were they regular policemen? If you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not regular policemen. Because the police also had a reserve force, which was trained in peace time for the mobilisation when it should occur, that is to increase the number of active police forces of the town of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: From your own knowledge, what sort of people joined this so-called special unit? If you know.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly soldiers who had done their military service in the military police. Those men received special training in peace time, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we just look, then, at this last bit of the video clip, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Dr. Nikola Koljevic, vice-president of the Republika Srpska, in his opening speech stated that the final goal was the creation of a union of Serbian states, but that at this stage we needed to take one step at a time and create joint institutions which were, at this moment, embodied in an association of assemblies, council of ministers, and a joint coordination body. During the debate, assemblymen also proposed a speedier course - unification of two Serbian states. Radoslav Brdjanin, Nedeljko Rasula, and Mitar Miljanovic asked that a decision on unification be adopted, so that voters could either confirm or reject it at the referendum. Dr. Radovan Karadzic stated that, despite the existing desire, this reality did not permit us to go forward immediately with unification. As Dr. Karadzic put it: 'It does not dawn before daybreak.' Assemblymen approved this explanation by a majority of votes and constituted a four-member commission comprising: Rajko Kasagic, Milovan Milanovic, Vojo Maksimovic, and Milan Trbojevic to prepare, in collaboration with the commission of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, documents needed for constituting the association of assemblies. The debate on resolution 820 was also quite heated, although practically no dissonant voices were heard. Dr. Radovan Karadzic stated that this resolution was unjust toward the Serbian people. 'It could even be said it was genocidal,' said Dr. Karadzic. Biljana Plavsic proposed that Dr. Radovan Karadzic give a report to the assemblymen on the political situation. General Ratko Mladic on the military one and Dr. Vladimir Lukic on the economic situation. She also proposed the assembly adopt in closed session two to three courses for further action in Republika Srpska. Aleksa Buha, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Republika Srpska, made a proposal, which was subsequently adopted, for the assembly to send a memorandum to the members of the European Union, Security Council, and the United Nations itemising all mistakes committed by European and international policy makers in resolving the crisis on the territory of the former and never-to-be-whole-again Bosnia and Herzegovina. Momcilo Krajisnik, president of the national assembly of Republika Srpska, gave us an assessment of the work conducted so far. "In addition to the resolution we discussed certain segments..."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop. Thank you. I do not need any more of the video. I don't think we need to see Mr. Krajisnik being interviewed. That's all I want to play on that video. Your Honour, we should say, as far as we can work out, because of the mention of the UN resolution 820, this was an assembly -- we can't date it exactly but in early 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But what I want to ask you about this, Colonel, and this leads me on to the final topic I want to ask you about and that's Brdjanin himself. We heard Brdjanin and others, Rasula from Sanski Most, that a decision on the unification of the two, as it were, Serbian states, the two Krajinas, was decided upon. Had you heard Brdjanin express views saying that the two, as it were, the Krajinas should be joined together in one Serbian state?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin's statement was carried by the media, both the Glas from Banja Luka, Banja Luka Television. I didn't listen to the radio, but I read it in the Banja Luka Glas.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you heard -- this is we think, 1993. Had you heard him express views earlier, either in 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not in 1991, but yes in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May that then be made Exhibit P1598 with the transcript as 1598-1, A and B?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Then I'd like to you look, please at one last document and that's a newspaper article in connection with Mr. Brdjanin. Could you be handed, please, the edition, it's 2.111 disclosure number, it's Glas, 19th of May and the headline is: "Fear of Imaginary Date." And under that it says, "Subject, the Autonomous Region of Krajina's war staff claims that there is no foundation for rumours about the war spreading around to Banja Luka." And it quotes Radoslav Brdjanin giving an explanation for the reasons surrounding various things that had been decided in respect of the 20th of May. And then he talks about the military recruits, "There was a heated debate at today's session concerning disarmament. The long debate following today's session of the Autonomous Region of Krajina's war staff clarified all the uncertainties about who would be responsible for how the confiscation of illegally-obtained weapons would be carried out. It was concluded that this difficult and extremely responsible task for the preservation of peace in these territories will be performed by members of the military and civilian police forces." And then it dealt with the political situation, and Mr. Bulic addressed them. And then "Predrag Radic, mayor of Banja Luka, and general Momir Talic commander of the Banja Luka Corps of the armed forces of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina told reporters about the latest conclusion from today's session of the Crisis Staff." And then I think there is a box where we see that this -- Talic speaking again. "The Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina proclaimed its army. All other armies that are not under its command or part of the police force we consider paramilitary and they must disarm. Because there cannot be two armies in the area where the Banja Luka or Krajina armies live and operate, said General Momir Talic, commander of the Banja Luka Corps." Now, this refers back to the meeting, again, of the 20th -- of the 18th of May that you recorded Talic telling his officers about in your workbook. I want now to deal with, as it were, the connections between Brdjanin and Talic. To your knowledge, how often would those two men meet? I don't mean the exact figure but on average.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know the exact number of their meetings, but they met regularly, to exchange information, both political and military. And the number of meetings was indicative of their close -- of the close ties between the politics and the army. Without their communication, there would be problems for the population and for the troops, and to my mind, it is -- it was natural for them to meet quite often.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How often did you yourself, during the period of 1992, attend meetings at which Brdjanin was present? You've already described, I think, one or -- no, two meetings. One with the UNPROFOR agenda, as to whether they were going to pay millions of dollars, and I think you described one other. I'm not sure. But anyhow, can I ask you, how often did you attend meetings at which he was present?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Other than those meetings, did you see him in the media, either on television or read about him in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often, almost daily.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that -- let's split that. On television, are you talking about, or the radio, or in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Banja Luka Glas, because it came out regularly, and in Banja Luka, there were frequent power cuts, especially in 1991 [as interpreted], we had serious problems with electricity so that I did not watch television all that often but whenever we had electricity, and he -- whenever I saw him, he was always explicitly requested the realisation of the ultimate objectives of the SDS and the Crisis Staff of Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a transcript problems that needs correcting. Page 44 line 7 the witness said 1992, not 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've had that one before, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Colonel, did you say with reference to frequent power cuts, were you referring to 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. That corrects the mistake in the transcript. Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You said that he -- whenever you saw him, in the media, he always explicitly requested the realisation of the ultimate objectives of the SDS and the Crisis Staff of Bosanska Krajina. What sort of influence did his speeches and his -- well, first of all, what sort of influence did his speeches have? How much influence did they carry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, again how would he know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He should be asked first whether he knows, and if so, how he knows, then he can say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair. So you just rephrase your question as to whether he is in a position to enlighten us on the information that you are seeking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, are you able to tell us, from your own knowledge, what kind of influence his speeches and the like carried?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: All Mr. Brdjanin's statements worried a great deal and frightened me, my friends, all Muslims and all Croats, because they all concluded from the statements that for them, there was -- it was impossible to go on living in Bosanska Krajina. He's a man who is president of the Crisis Staff, who has the authority on behalf of the SDS and on behalf of the Crisis Staff, and we used to comment it, in all our contacts with the citizens in Banja Luka, I mean Croats and Bosniaks. My colleagues, officers, I mean Serbs, clearly commented on Mr. Brdjanin's words and statements only in the affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, we know that there were running in tandem the Regional Crisis Staff headed by Mr. Brdjanin, as the President, and the Banja Luka Municipal Crisis Staff headed by Mr. Radic, who was president of the Municipal Assembly. Of the two of them, which was the more important, as far as you and the army were concerned, first of all?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the army, Mr. Brdjanin was more important. However, for the town of Banja Luka, Predrag Radic, the mayor of the municipality, was more important.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was the difference? Why was Mr. Brdjanin more important for the army and Mr. Radic more important for the town of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff covered Bosanska Krajina as such, its whole territory. And the army used all the human resources and all the material resources, and -- but the army always had to go through the Crisis Staff, through the Regional Crisis Staff. And Mr. Predrag Radic was responsible only for the town of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, thank you very much indeed. That's all I ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be P1599, this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Article, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Colonel, you are now going to be cross-examined by Mr. Ackerman, who is the lead counsel in defence of the accused Mr. Brdjanin. It's almost unnecessary for me, but I will just remind you that you have absolutely no right to distinguish between the Defence and the Prosecution when it comes to questions and answers. Your duty is to answer all the questions that Mr. Ackerman will be putting to you, as truthfully and as fully as you can. That is in accordance with the solemn undertaking that you made in the beginning of your testimony and which you repeated every day. That's of course unless we tell you not to answer any particular question that is put to you or we stop Mr. Ackerman from proceeding with certain questions. But short of that, your duty is to answer all the questions, because Mr. Ackerman here is doing his duty. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Ackerman:

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel, almost good evening, I guess I could say.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have a lot of material to cover with you, and it would be helpful, in terms of time, if you could listen very carefully to the questions that I ask you and try your best to answer them. Some of them you can answer easily with a yes or no. If they require any kind of explanation, try to make it as brief and to the point as possible. And that way, we'll finish maybe sometime tomorrow. Okay?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just have some kind of general questions on a number of subjects I want to start with. And I want to begin kind of where Ms. Korner began with you, and that is the significance of the date 18 May, 1992. After that date, which was the date that the JNA became the VRS, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: After that date, you stayed in the service?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And actually became an officer of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, but I applied for retirement on the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you wore on your uniform the insignia of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN SELAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
